title: require, require_relative, and Code Loading
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of require, require_relative, and code loading in a Ruby program and name the key rule involved.
Apply require, require_relative, and code loading in a small example and predict its result before running it.
Identify one boundary or failure case related to avoiding accidental duplicate execution and verify the intended behavior.

content.intro: Learn require, require_relative, and Code Loading through a visual model, a minimal Ruby example, and a practical check.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding require, require_relative, and code loading helps you write code that is easier to explain, test, and maintain. It also helps separate Ruby language guarantees from runtime assumptions, dependency behavior, and application-specific rules.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: require, require_relative, and Code Loading helps you reason about loading files. In Ruby, prefer a small example whose inputs and expected result are easy to explain. This lesson connects the syllabus topic to practical code and highlights where assumptions or edge cases matter.

content_blocks.title: How to think about it
content_blocks.text: Begin by identifying the key rule: Loading files. Then connect it to Reusing libraries. The remaining syllabus points—Avoiding accidental duplicate execution—are useful checks before applying this in a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Recap
